An optimal power flow (OPF) problem quantifies the deficiency of a candidate portfolio by optimizing the dispatch of controllable devices and measuring thermal and voltage violations on a common scale, with an optimal value of zero exactly at adequate portfolios. The OPF multipliers give a first-order approximation of the relief each investment candidate would provide. We bound the error of this approximation and show that structural properties of the deficiency guard it against overestimation. Building on this property, a heuristic cutting-plane search uses a mixed-integer linear program to propose each next portfolio from these approximations. On six unbalanced three-phase feeders from the SMART-DS dataset, the search outperforms a linearized optimization-based benchmark, and the results agree across five variants of the deficiency.

title: Wing Rock Modeling and Control for Flight-Critical Systems
abstract: Aircraft equipped with delta wings are designed to be aerodynamically efficient in high-speed flight. However, at low-speed flight conditions with sufficiently high angle of attack, these vehicles often have lightly damped, close to unstable lateral-directional dynamics, such as the dutch roll mode. As a result, a delta wing aircraft often exhibits the so-called wing rock (WR) phenomenon, with a back and forth rocking motion, while the aircraft sideslip angle, the roll and the yaw angular rates remain small. In this paper, the WR dynamics are defined as a lightly damped dutch roll mode excited by airmass vortical external input, acting at or near the dutch roll natural frequency. The vortical signal comes from Fourier-Galerkin approximation of the Navier-Stokes equation, with no-penetration boundary conditions and the resulting airmass velocities are calculated by the Lorenz dynamical system of three coupled bilinear ordinary differential equations. In that context, the Lorenz bilinear dynamics become the disturbance-generator exosystem, acting on the lightly damped lateral-directional aircraft mode at or near its natural frequency, and thus exciting it to produce near oscillatory wing rocking motion. Using the proposed model, a flight control design trade study is conducted to mitigate and suppress the WR phenomenon.

title: Multi-Agent Deferred-Decision Trajectory Optimization with Anytime-Valid Target Retention for Moving Candidates
abstract: We study multi-agent terminal interception when one of several moving candidates is the unknown target and both target identity and candidate terminal locations are uncertain. We develop a receding-horizon deferred-decision trajectory optimization (DDTO) controller that combines conformal terminal-location prediction, sequential candidate rejection, capacity-constrained assignment, and candidate-contingent planning. Under exchangeability conditions for terminal and identity residuals, with predictable querying, we establish fixed-time terminal-location coverage and anytime-valid target retention. At the final replan, when one control step remains, we bound the joint probability that a tightened-set DDTO plan passes nonlinear rollout verification but capture fails. The closed-loop controller applies fallback guidance to any agent without a verified DDTO plan and, across 100 paired scenarios, captures 79% of targets under the strict control-effort budget and 85% when that budget is relaxed.

title: Decision-Making in Digital Twins: Optimization, Control, and Learning
abstract: A digital twin is a virtual representation of a physical system, continuously updated with data from the physical system, enabling dynamic information exchange and decision-making. This bidirectional interaction, which distinguishes digital twins from conventional simulation models, introduces new challenges to simulation-based optimization, control, and learning. This paper reviews recent developments in decision-making methodologies motivated by digital twins. We focus on three interconnected areas: simulation optimization, sequential decision making, and risk-aware decision making. For simulation optimization, we discuss data-driven simulation optimization under input uncertainty, streaming input data, decision-dependent observations, and limited computational and data-collection resources. For sequential decision making, we review the connections among digital twins, stochastic optimal control, and reinforcement learning, with emphasis on Bayesian approaches that update models and policies as new information becomes available. For risk-aware decision making, we discuss distributionally robust and Bayesian risk formulations as alternative approaches for addressing model uncertainty. Throughout the paper, we emphasize the common problem of making decisions while the underlying model is being updated. We conclude by identifying research challenges and opportunities.

title: A Power-Trajectory Framework for Data Center Participation in Day-Ahead Markets
abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) is driving substantial growth in data center electricity demand. Interval-based energy blocks in day-ahead markets do not explicitly retain predictable intra-interval demand evolution, potentially creating mismatches with ramp-feasible generation trajectories and affecting settlement. This paper proposes a power-trajectory framework in which data centers declare predictable aggregate demand evolution through continuous demand-side power trajectories before market clearing. The declared trajectories are treated as exogenous inputs for constructing generation trajectories and the corresponding price trajectory. For feasible market-clearing outcomes, physical temporal consistency is established through continuous-time power balance and satisfaction of the modeled generation operating constraints, while economic temporal consistency is established by preserving the dispatch-price correspondence in energy settlement on a common temporal basis. Under the adopted settlement definitions, a trajectory-based settlement analysis separately quantifies the monetary magnitude of representation-induced power imbalances and the supply-side compensation that may remain under temporally consistent clearing and settlement. An illustrative 5-bus case demonstrates the elimination of representation-induced power imbalance and identifies the timing and physical sources of supply-side compensation. A modified IEEE RTS-GMLC case further illustrates these compensation effects across multiple generating units under workload-driven data center demand variations.

title: Counterfactual Action-Conditioned Graph Prediction for Cascading-Failure Mitigation in Power Systems
abstract: Cascading failures develop through coupled power flow redistribution, protection actions, and topology changes, making remedial control dependent on how alternative interventions modify the subsequent trajectory. This paper develops an action-conditioned graph predictor (ACGP) for multi-step cascade prediction and closed-loop mitigation. A same-state counterfactual branching procedure replays identical post-contingency grid states under multiple legal actions while preserving the exogenous trajectory, providing direct supervision for action-dependent electrical states, line connectivity, automatic protection trips, and terminal risk. ACGP is embedded in a receding-horizon controller that evaluates five-step candidate futures, executes the selected intervention, and replans from the observed next state. The final dataset contains 2,860 counter factual roots and 22,880 action-conditioned branches. On the held-out test set, ACGP achieves a five-step line-loading MAE of 0.0369 and a redispatch pairwise ranking accuracy of 0.806; action ablations reduce the ranking accuracy to approximately chance level. In closed-loop Grid2Op experiments, terminal-failure and cascade rates decrease from 53.3% and 51.1% under do-nothing operation to 12.2% and 7.8%, respectively, close to the simulator-reference values of 11.1% and 6.7%. The results show that same-state counterfactual prediction can support effective action comparison and feedback-based cascading-failure mitigation.

title: Controller-Agnostic Runtime Safety Certificates for Tool-Using AI Agents via Data-Driven Robust Reachability
abstract: Software agents built on large language models act by issuing tool calls, some of which cannot be undone. To control theory the model is an opaque feedback controller, replaced every few months, whose closed loop cannot be analyzed directly. We propose a runtime filter, or shield, between any such controller and its environment that certifies a bound on the probability of reaching an unsafe condition during a bounded task. Given a predicate abstraction and candidate successor sets, everything else comes from logs: the loop becomes a finite controlled Markov chain, the estimated kernel is surrounded by a distribution-free confidence region, and robust reach-avoid value iteration runs over it. The certificate is probably approximately correct and uniform over controllers respecting the filter, so one model may replace another without recomputation. In all tested datasets the true risk stayed within certificate and budget; in a file-system sandbox the filter stays sound against a hazard the logs barely covered, where a plug-in baseline certifies safety and fails; and it holds seven controllers, three of them open-weights models, to zero unsafe outcomes in 1050 episodes.

title: Venusian Radio Occultation Constellation Design and Reconfiguration Problems: A Benders Decomposition Approach
abstract: Driven by the scientific value of Venusian atmospheric studies, numerous missions, such as Magellan and Venus Express, have relied on single-spacecraft radio occultation (RO) experiments. Despite their proven success, data throughput is inherently limited by the use of a single transmitter and its relative geometry with respect to Earth-based receivers. Therefore, the literature proposes leveraging a constellation of spacecraft to increase RO measurement opportunities and improve spatial and temporal coverage; however, current efforts impose strict simplifying assumptions that limit their applicability and responsiveness to complex mission narratives. Beyond initial constellation design, evolving mission objectives may require event-based constellation reconfiguration during operations. To address both design and operational needs, we propose two problems formulated as integer linear programs: the RO Constellation Configuration Design Problem and the RO Constellation Reconfiguration Problem. Further, we address the programs' solution-space explosion with a Benders decomposition approach. Numerical experiments show the applicability of our problems for constellation configuration design, tackle the full mission pipeline, transitioning from global atmospheric profiling to on-demand regional profiling above areas of volcanic interest, and show that the Benders decomposition approach efficiently obtains high-quality solutions to large-scale instances.

title: DCCB-Capability-Aware Optimal Info-Power Flow for Transmission Switching in AC/MTDC Grids
abstract: Transmission switching is an effective approach for restoring operational flexibility and improving the economic performance of AC/multi-terminal DC (MTDC) grids following DC-side faults. Its practical implementation requires that the faulted branch be safely isolated and that the associated switching commands be successfully delivered through the communication network. However, conventional transmission switching models generally represent switching actions using binary variables, without considering the availability of communication resources or whether the corresponding DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) can interrupt the fault current affected by time delay. To address these issues, this paper develops an explicit optimal info--power flow (OIPF) formulation that incorporates information transmission into the post-fault transmission-switching optimization for AC/MTDC grids. The switching status of each DC branch is determined by the availability of its communication path and associated communication resources. In addition, binary switching decisions are supplemented by a DCCB feasibility constraint that limits the estimated delayed-interruption current to the DCCB breaking capability. The resulting problem is formulated as a mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) model that can be efficiently solved using off-the-shelf optimization solvers. Numerical results reveal that limited communication capacity and additional routing costs may render electrically beneficial switching actions infeasible or uneconomical, while delay-aware DCCB interruption constraints may favor lower-delay communication routes despite their higher costs.

title: Safeguarding Intelligent Power Dispatch:A Performance-Equivalent-Model-Based Safety-Critical Control Method for DC Microgrids
abstract: Intelligent power dispatch is enabling fast and self-adaptive decision-making in microgrids, yet its deployment in real-world industry remains limited due to unresolved safety concerns. Existing safety-preserving approaches typically rely on an accurate characterization of the feasible operating region, which is impossible to obtain under uncertain and heterogeneous system dynamics. Moreover, even a dispatch command verified as feasible at a discrete setpoint may become unsafe during its continuous physical execution. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a safety-aware dispatch adjustment framework that uses performance-equivalent modeling of closed-loop systems (PEM-CLS) and embeds high-order control barrier functions and control Lyapunov functions within a quadratic programming formulation (HOCBF-CLF-QP). PEM-CLS captures EMS-required power-regulation dynamics solely from port-level responses, without requiring internal subsystem models, parameters, or controller information. Its modeling error is analytically characterized and explicitly bounded, enabling requirement-oriented dynamic abstraction for safety-critical control. Based on these PEMs, the HOCBF-CLF-QP safety controller coordinates heterogeneous transient power responses and corrects unsafe EMS commands to maintain dynamic safety during command execution. Four deliberately constructed extreme stress-test scenarios are used to expose conflicts between nominal EMS commands and physical safety. Without intervention, the DC-bus voltage violates its safety limit in all four cases, whereas the proposed framework maintains QP feasibility and limits the voltage deviation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an algorithm-agnostic safety execution layer for intelligent power dispatch without requiring an exact feasible-region model or detailed internal information of lower-level devices.

title: NANO: A Unified Optimization Framework for Nonlinear Gaussian Filtering
abstract: Conventional Gaussian filtering typically approximates nonlinear models or their statistical moments and retains the Kalman update structure. The resulting approximation errors can affect both state estimates and their uncertainty. This paper presents the Natural Gradient Gaussian Approximation (NANO) framework for nonlinear filtering. Both prediction and measurement update are formulated as optimization problems over Gaussian distributions, with the entire Gaussian distribution serving as the optimization variable. The framework integrates observation losses, distributional discrepancies, natural-gradient optimization, and finite-step update rules, providing a unified formulation for constructing different filters. Natural-gradient iterations account for the geometry of the Gaussian family and jointly update the distribution parameters. The framework incorporates the existing NANO-P method using the Kullback-Leibler divergence and introduces NANO-W using the Wasserstein distance. NANO-P maintains covariance positive definiteness through a positive-semidefinite curvature approximation, while NANO-W uses a covariance transport update that accommodates indefinite curvature. Their update rules and sufficient conditions for covariance positive definiteness are established within the common framework. Through these two realizations, the proposed framework achieves the best estimation accuracy among the evaluated methods on each of six benchmarks. Runtime evaluations further assess its computational feasibility for practical applications.

title: Scalable Identification of Physics-Based and Neural Dynamics from Partial Measurements
abstract: We present a scalable method for identifying nonlinear dynamics from partial measurements, supporting physics-based, neural-network, and gray-box models. We use the Prediction Error Method (PEM) coupled with state estimation performed by a Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) scheme, which can account directly for general nonlinear dynamics. This results in a bi-level optimization problem that scales poorly with increasing model parameters. To improve computational efficiency, we derive a reformulation that avoids explicit parameter-wide sensitivity matrices and exploits the temporal structure of the underlying optimization problem. Numerical comparisons show up to a $215\times$ speedup in hypergradient evaluation. Racing-vehicle simulations demonstrate accurate prediction and physical-parameter recovery in tire-force identification. Real-world data show that the gray-box model improves prediction accuracy with a neural residual while retaining physical interpretability.

title: Design of Privacy-Preserving Estimators Under Prior Information Exposure
abstract: State estimation is widely used in networked dynamical systems, but released estimates may inadvertently reveal sensitive information about private state variables. Existing privacy-preserving estimation frameworks often do not explicitly account for adversarial prior knowledge. Motivated by this gap, we study privacy-preserving state estimation for discrete-time linear stochastic systems under prior information exposure using pointwise maximal leakage (PML). We first reveal a privacy anti-optimality property of the Kalman filter: in the absence of additive release noise, the steady-state Kalman filter maximizes PML privacy leakage among the considered class of stable linear estimators. We further establish a nontrivial lower bound on the steady-state estimation error enforced by $(\varepsilon,δ)$-PML privacy. We then derive sufficient release-noise conditions that guarantee $(\varepsilon,δ)$-PML privacy, first for the Kalman filter and then for stable linear estimators. Finally, a convex semidefinite program is formulated for a joint design of the estimator gain and release noise covariance, providing a tractable privacy-preserving estimator with an explicit upper bound on the steady-state estimation error. Simulations on a source--load power system demonstrate the proposed privacy--utility tradeoff.

title: Aerodynamic Promptness of Tilting-Propeller Multirotors
abstract: This work develops a geometric theory of aerodynamic promptness for multirotor platforms whose propeller directions depend on a smooth orientation-mechanism configuration. The actuator state consists of the actual signed propeller speeds and the mechanism configuration, and the nonlinear actuator map retains both the signed-quadratic propeller law and the configuration-dependent thrust directions. Constant direction maps represent fixed propellers, while shared dependence on mechanism coordinates represents mechanically coupled tilts. A Riemannian metric on the product actuator manifold compares propeller accelerations and orientation-mechanism rates through physically interpretable scales. Composing the actuator-map differential, the musical isomorphism induced by this metric, and the dual differential defines a task-rate authority map from wrench covectors to wrench-rate vectors. In fixed task coordinates, the square root of the determinant of its matrix defines aerodynamic promptness. Positive promptness is equivalent to local wrench-rate surjectivity, while the associated spectrum resolves directional authority and conditioning. The same construction yields the metric horizontal inverse, the orthogonal projector onto wrench-fiber directions, and task-preserving internal motions that regulate promptness without changing the instantaneous wrench. The construction is related intrinsically to dynamic feedback linearization and specialized to the independently tilting, radially arranged Holocopter and Voliro architectures, clarifying how their established allocation and rank constructions fit within the same actuator-manifold geometry.

title: Learning Reachability-Based Safety Representations for Real-Time Robot Navigation in Unknown and Dynamic Environments
abstract: Safe robot navigation in unknown, dynamic environments requires more than geometric collision checking: a robot still far from an obstacle may be unable to avoid it because of its speed, orientation, or the obstacle's motion. Hamilton--Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis captures this in a value function whose sign separates states that admit a safe continuation from those where collision is unavoidable, but computing it online for every newly observed environment is too expensive. This dissertation trains neural implicit representations offline on reachability solutions to give optimization-based controllers this information in real time. Since the value function never exceeds the constraint, it equals a directly computed constraint, such as a signed distance, minus a nonnegative dynamics correction. Learning only this correction keeps represented obstacles outside the predicted safe set despite approximation errors. The first two of five methods use the learned function as a terminal constraint in model predictive control, for static local environments and predicted obstacle motion. The next two use it as a barrier candidate in control barrier function safety filters, for static environments and, through pairwise barriers in relative coordinates, for a varying number of moving obstacles. Simulations and hardware experiments on ground and aerial robots show better collision avoidance than geometric and hand-designed baselines, especially for short horizons and moving obstacles. The fifth method replaces the grid-based offline solver, which limits the first four to low-dimensional models. For control-affine dynamics with polytopic inputs, the HJ Hamiltonian is maximized at a vertex, so a parallelizable tree search over vertex inputs can generate training labels. With a loss from the HJ variational inequality, these labels yield barrier candidates for systems with up to 13 states.

title: Towards learning-enhanced solvers for multi-parametric optimization
abstract: Neural networks (NNs) have been employed in various ways to accelerate the solution of multi-parametric optimization problems (OPs), which prominently arise in model predictive control (MPC). Early approaches focused on approximating the parametric solution (e.g., the optimal control law) directly by NNs. More recently, learning-based techniques have been used to emulate or enhance solver iterations. For the direct approximation of the parametric solution, it has been demonstrated that exploiting structural properties of the underlying OP facilitates the design of suitable NN architectures. In this paper, we show that structural analysis can also be leveraged to systematically integrate learning into classical optimization algorithms, thereby enhancing their performance. We formalize our concept for the case of multi-parametric quadratic programs (mpQPs), which frequently arise in linear-quadratic MPC, as a representative application. More precisely, we demonstrate that tailored NNs enable a parameter-dependent fine-tuning of the step sizes in a standard dual projected gradient scheme. The design of the NNs is guided by the observation that optimal step sizes, which permit obtaining the exact optimal solution in finitely many iterations, are piecewise constant functions over the parameter space (e.g., the state space in MPC). We establish key theoretical properties of the proposed approach and illustrate its effectiveness in a numerical case study.

title: Geometric Transition of Latent Dynamics in Intermittent Chaos: SVD-based Effective Dimension for Detection and Proactive Control
abstract: This paper investigates the geometric detection of latent dynamic transitions (where the latent space is defined as a finite-dimensional state space reconstructed via a delay-embedding Hankel matrix) in mutually coupled phase-locked loops (PLLs) exhibiting on-off intermittent chaos. We propose a data-driven approach to identify the transition of the effective dimension in latent dynamics as a precursor to physical bursting events. By applying Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to a Hankel matrix constructed from high-resolution oversampled data, we extract the effective dimension that reflects the dynamical shift of intrinsic variables - from a synchronized two-dimensional manifold to a higher-dimensional chaotic state - prior to the actual burst. This geometric indicator enables a proactive, event-driven intervention using Pyragas-type delayed feedback control, which is activated only when the detected dimension exceeds a critical threshold. Simulation results demonstrate that this geometric precursor effectively compensates for control latencies and substantially reduces accumulated control energy compared to conventional continuous feedback. The findings establish a methodological strategy for stabilizing infinite-dimensional delayed systems by exploiting early warning signals embedded in dimensional transitions of latent dynamics.

title: Equilibria and consensus in discrete-time opinion dynamics with mixed weighted-averaging and weighted-median mechanisms
abstract: Opinion dynamics models relate interpersonal influence to consensus or persistent disagreement. We study a discrete-time model combining weighted-average and weighted-median updates on a fixed directed network. Individuals update synchronously with possibly different adjustment coefficients. We characterize equilibria through local balance conditions and opinion level sets, and establish convergence to a Lyapunov-stable equilibrium using nonexpansiveness and Krasnosel'skii--Mann theory. We define type-dependent cohesive sets: each weighted-average member assigns all its weight to the set, whereas each weighted-median member assigns at least one half. Consensus is reached from every initial condition if and only if no two such sets are disjoint. Otherwise, an open set of initial conditions leads to persistent disagreement. Replacing weighted-median individuals by weighted-average individuals preserves consensus whenever it is already guaranteed for all initial conditions. Four numerical studies examine the number and locations of weighted-average individuals. The frequency of reaching a prescribed consensus tolerance is nondecreasing with their fraction in the sampled ensembles, but individual realizations need not follow this trend.

title: $H_2$-optimal model order reduction using hyperbolic geometry
abstract: We revisit the problem of approximating a linear time-invariant LTI model by a reduced-order model (ROM) in an $H_2$-optimal sense. A widely used method for computing such ROMs is the iterative rational Krylov algorithm (IRKA). However, in practice, the stability of the resulting ROM is not generally guaranteed. In this work, we develop a novel framework that can be used to obtain $H_2$-optimal models of single-input single-output LTI systems while enforcing stability of the ROM. We use Malmquist-Takenaka orthogonal expansions in the corresponding $H_2$-spaces and their connection to hyperbolic geometry to develop an equilibrium function. We show that the poles of an $H_2$-optimal ROM transfer function are defined by the zeros of this equilibrium function. The resulting nonlinear root-finding problem is solved using a Newton-type method formulated on the products of Poincaré disk manifolds, where updates are performed along hyperbolic geodesics ensuring that the stability constraint is satisfied at every iteration. We present numerical experiments on benchmark systems for both discrete- and continuous-time LTI MOR problems, including examples where IRKA produces unstable reduced models while the proposed method preserves stability throughout the iteration.

title: Event-Driven Safe Control of a Black-Box Balancing Wheel with Friction-Gated Actuation
abstract: Commercial balancing wheels are closed systems: an internal controller keeps the board upright, and a rider steers by shifting weight and twisting the hips. We augment a one-wheel with a lead-screw weight shift for longitudinal motion and a reaction wheel for yaw. The reaction wheel stores limited momentum, so a turn is a sequence of torque pulses, and whether a pulse rotates the body depends on static friction at the tire contact. From a 24-pulse torque sweep on one surface we fit a two-part model that gives the probability that a pulse rotates the body, treating the breakaway torque as random, and the rotation angle when it does; at maximum torque the posterior engagement probability is 0.54 (90% credible interval 0.24-0.84). The weight shift is modeled as a rate- limited input with a measured speed gain and an assumed first-order response, which predicts stopping distances four times those of a direct-force model. These models drive an event-triggered supervisor that schedules pulses by expected heading improvement, brakes when the predicted braking path would leave the safe set, tightens margins for model uncertainty, and updates the friction estimate online. In simulation on 500 plants drawn from the fitted models, the robust supervisor completed 92.6% of missions with 1.8% safety violations and 1.6% safe aborts, versus 84.0% and 7.2% for a supervisor using mean models and 1.8% and 20.4% for a baseline that ignores friction. A video of the hardware experiments is available online (https://github.com/ASAS-Labs/x-wheel).

title: CIPHEUR: LLM-Guided Structural Search Control for Conflict-Graph Optimization
abstract: Conflict-graph search can stagnate despite effective operators when interventions fail to address the conflicts blocking progress. A disruptive intervention may also require further search before its value emerges. We propose CIPHEUR, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that connects conflict evidence to coordinated intervention and recovery through Structured Intervention Units (SIUs). The shared control interface supports offline synthesis of executable policies and online contextual decisions. Asynchronous online control sustains native search during inference, while all policies preserve the original objective and feasibility constraints. Across eight satellite-ground scheduling conflict views with five runs per view and a 900-second evaluation cap, CIPHEUR-online achieves the highest mean objective among 11 configurations and increases mean scheduled contact duration by 14.84% over the greedy baseline GWMIN. It exceeds the strongest external per-view mean in seven of eight views and outperforms CHILS in all 40 paired runs. Within the same runs, its normalized objective improvement from 360 to 900 seconds is 1.50 to 1.86 times that of the two programmatic controllers. A separately frozen, one-shot LLM-generated controller also improves the mean objective over CHILS without runtime model calls. Together, these results demonstrate how structural search control translates LLM design knowledge and contextual reasoning into improved solution quality and sustained search progress.

title: Adaptive Calibration of Day-Ahead Flexibility Reserve Requirements Under Distribution Shift
abstract: The increasing integration of variable renewable generation introduces weather-driven variability and uncertainty into power-system operations. System operators manage the resulting deviations between day-ahead forecasts and real-time net load by scheduling upward and downward flexibility reserves. These requirements have traditionally been set using simple deterministic rules. Newer data-driven methods tailor reserves to forecasts and operating conditions. However, their reliability may deteriorate when conditions depart from the historical data. We address this limitation with a sequential framework that updates day-ahead reserve requirements as operating outcomes become available. Within this framework, Adaptive Conformal Inference targets the frequency of insufficient reserve, whereas Rolling Risk Control targets expected uncovered deviation, the mean residual beyond the scheduled reserve. We prove finite-horizon bounds on realized miscoverage and capped uncovered-deviation loss. We test the framework on real ERCOT data in a chronological deployment simulation that respects operational timing: outcomes from one day first affect the reserve schedule two days later. Training and validation use 2022--2023 data; the uninterrupted test covers 2024--2025. Coverage calibration achieves approximately 90% coverage, with upward and downward miscoverage near 5%. Risk calibration brings expected uncovered deviations close to their budgets while using 5.3% less reserve than the uncalibrated requirements. The framework thus produces adaptive reserve requirements that provably control the selected reliability metrics over finite horizons without assuming stationarity or exchangeability.

title: AC-Aware Steady-State Security Region Characterization via Exclusion Refinement
abstract: As active power dispatch becomes increasingly coupled with reactive power support and voltage security in modern power systems, AC security regions (AC-SRs) under exact steady-state AC power flow (AC-PF) constraints provide valuable insights into admissible operating boundaries and security margins for security assessment. However, the nonconvexity of exact AC-PF constraints makes it difficult to achieve both accuracy and computational efficiency in AC-SR characterization. To this end, this paper proposes an AC-aware iterative exclusion refinement (AC-ITER) approach that refines a given convex-relaxed AC-SR toward the exact AC-SR by progressively constructing and removing convexlocal exclusion subregions around numerically identified insecure points. Boundary-point searches and dual-based local exclusion cuts provide a tractable approximation of relaxation-induced insecure portions. A statistical certification method based on uniform sampling is developed to support high-confidence assessment of residual-region security and guide termination, while an AC-PF security similarity-based acceleration (AC-SSA) approach is introduced to further accelerate the sampling-based search for insecure operating points. Numerical studies on academic test systems and real-world systems demonstrate the characterization accuracy of AC-ITER and the computational efficiency gained through AC-SSA.

title: Distributed Observation Scheduling and Sensor Fusion For Large Agile Constellations
abstract: With the rapid increase in interest towards large scale earth observing satellite constellations, the problem of properly commanding and utilizing these systems has become increasingly relevant. This work focuses on a complete distributed approach to this problem, incorporating an observation task allocation and scheduling algorithm in addition to a sensor data fusion algorithm for end-to-end target coverage and processing. Observation task allocation and scheduling is performed in this work through the combination of the bid warped consensus based bundle algorithm (BWCBBA) and a lightweight observation scheduler for bid scoring. This method produces a unique mapping of tasks to command agents when allowed to iterate sufficiently. The approach to distributed data fusion in this work occurs primarily through an ownership model in which one satellite takes ownership of a system track in the constellation. After local information is shared between the sensing nodes to create the system tracks, the dedicated fusion nodes assume ownership for further information fusion and track information is disseminated throughout the constellation for data association. This paper analyzes the performance of these two algorithms over a set of increasingly decentralized architectures to highlight the performance losses compared to more traditional centralized methods.

title: Physics-guided machine learning for saturation control across variable hydraulic conditions in heap leaching
abstract: Heap-leaching hydraulics vary between regions of an ore bed, motivating fast prediction models that accommodate different material properties. This study develops a parameter-conditioned physics-guided machine-learning (PGML) surrogate and demonstrates its use in simulated saturation control. A dataset of 4096 numerical Richards-equation trajectories was divided into 2867 training, 614 validation and 615 evaluation cases. The network predicts hourly saturation profiles from the current profile, irrigation rate and four hydraulic parameters, and is trained with an approximate Gardner mass-balance penalty. A daily predictive controller compared 200 constant irrigation rates over a 24-hour horizon. Across the evaluation cases, the median full-cycle tracking deviation was 4.9% of a 0.70 saturation target, equal to that of a tuned proportional-integral (PI) controller, while the PGML controller reached the target without overshoot in the median and applied approximately 4% less irrigation. Moderate physics guidance reduced long-horizon prediction error by approximately 30% relative to data-only training and reduced irrigation-bound activity, but slightly worsened closed-loop tracking. For a matched prediction workload, the surrogate was approximately 70 times faster than the numerical solver, and batched evaluation cost under 2 ms per column for 5000 columns. The results support a reusable physics-guided surrogate for large-scale saturation control in simulation.

title: Rayleigh-Benard Stabilization by Fredholm Backstepping
abstract: Among Navier--Stokes systems, the Rayleigh--Bénard layer, a fluid between two horizontal plates heated from below and cooled from above, is the benchmark of hydrodynamic instability that manifests itself as the unsteady convection phenomenon, which in turn can be interpreted as the onset of chaos: the Lorenz equations represent the Fourier--Galerkin approximation coefficients for the minimal three-mode truncation of it. Its instability has no mean flow behind it. The fluid is at rest, the velocity and the temperature are each stable alone, and buoyancy closes a positive loop between them. The linearization is self-adjoint, its unstable spectrum real, and the number of unstable modes grows without bound in the Rayleigh number; at $\Ra=10^6$ the layer has $85$ of them, with growth rates up to $2137$. We stabilize the conductive state at every Rayleigh and Prandtl number, with any prescribed decay rate, by explicit feedback of the full state to the tangential velocity, temperature, and normal velocity of the upper plate. The feedback laws are obtained by Fredholm backstepping of the coupled velocity--temperature system, with pole placement for the lowest modes.

title: Jacobian State Augmented Viable Kinematic Safety Filter
abstract: Safety Filters (SF) are leveraged to design certifiably safe controllers, which ensures forward invariance on a defined safe set when the filter is feasible. Predictive Safety Filters (PSF) embed these constraints to a closed-loop model-based optimization method to improve constraint satisfaction, and reduce feasibility loss caused by myopic, one-step filtering. Related viability-based methods emphasize approximating a viability kernel which ensures admissible control for all future time, but requires significant computational expense. This work introduces a Jacobian-based kinematic safety filter leveraging an augmented state variable with task-space velocity and filters task-space acceleration to preserve the feasibility of a low-level filter while enforcing joint position and velocity. The proposed method introduces a nested Quadratic Program (QP) formulation, defines a conservative inner approximation of viability envelope and computes a viable planner online. The method is validated in a simplified 2R planar manipulator simulation environment and shows significant improvement compared to a baseline Control Barrier Function Quadratic Program (CBF-QP) based filter. The experiments highlights the improvements in terms of computation time compared to traditional PSF and Reference Governor approach while also showing significant reduction in feasibility violations. Lastly, a simplified demonstration on a simulated 6-DoF manipulator highlights the potential scalability of the method to higher degree-of-freedom setups.

title: Efficient Hybrid Hard--Soft Signal Temporal Logic MPC for Driving under Multimodal Uncertainty
abstract: Motion planning for automated vehicles in interactive traffic has to simultaneously ensure safety, respect traffic rules, and maintain comfortable progress under multi-modal behavior uncertainty. Imposing all these requirements as hard constraints reduces feasibility, whereas treating them all as costs allows safety-critical requirements to be traded against progress. We propose a hybrid hard--soft Signal Temporal Logic (STL) MPC framework that optimizes a single shared ego trajectory against every retained behavior hypothesis: minimum-distance and speed predicates are imposed as explicit hard constraints, while soft STL robustness terms shape clearance, comfort, and interaction quality within the resulting feasible driving corridor. This retains robustness to discrete interaction modes without branch-specific contingent ego policies. We further identify substantial symbolic graph-construction overhead and introduce reachability-certified relevance screening and vectorized symbolic construction to reduce computational cost while preserving the feasible set and objective. Closed-loop Monte Carlo evaluation over six highway and intersection scenarios shows the highest strict success rate among the compared planners with no observed collisions or rule violations, at roughly a quarter of the planning latency of the unoptimized formulation. An ablation study separates the two layers: the hard constraints define the safety envelope, while the soft terms improve clearance and motion quality within it.

title: Singular Sampling in Nonlinear Observability: Higher-Order Minimax Laws and Timing Crossovers
abstract: We study deterministic bounded-noise state reconstruction for nonlinear systems when the measurement schedule drives the sampled-output map through a rank-deficient configuration. Local reconstruction is governed by the leading pairwise separation order and its corresponding higher-order modulus, which together determine the leading minimax noise-to-state law. For corank-one cubic singular schedules, including overdetermined sampled maps, we derive the exact physical $\ell_\infty$ cubic modulus through quotient geometry in $\mathbb{R}^q/\operatorname{Im}DF$ and show how the required finite jet is computed from trajectory sensitivities. We then prove a uniform signed timing crossover: a transversal timing perturbation has transition scale $\varepsilon=O(δ^{2/3})$, linking the regular, cubic-singular, and fold regimes. A damped pendulum provides closed-form crossover coefficients and exact nonlinear minimax validation, while a four-state downward cart--pole verifies the rectangular theory. The results show that measurement timing can change not only reconstruction conditioning but the exponent governing bounded-noise state uncertainty.

title: Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with early and locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer.
abstract: The European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with early and locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were published in August 2025 and were adapted in November 2025 according to previously established standard methodology to produce the Pan-Asian adapted ESMO consensus guidelines for the management of Asian patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC. The adapted guidelines presented in this article represent the consensus opinions reached by a panel of Asian experts on the treatment of patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC representing the oncological societies of China (Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology), Indonesia (Indonesian Society of Hematology and Medical Oncology), India (Indian Society of Medical and Paediatric Oncology), Japan [Japanese Society of Medical Oncology (JSMO)], South Korea (Korean Society of Medical Oncology), Malaysia (Malaysian Oncological Society), the Philippines (Philippine Society of Medical Oncology), Singapore (Singapore Society of Oncology), Taiwan (Taiwan Oncology Society) and Thailand (Thai Society of Clinical Oncology), coordinated by ESMO and JSMO. The voting was based on scientific evidence and was independent of the current treatment practices, drug access restrictions and reimbursement decisions in the different regions of Asia. The latter are discussed separately in the article. The aim is to provide guidance for the optimisation and harmonisation of the management of patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC across the different countries of Asia, drawing on the evidence provided by both Western and Asian trials. Attention is drawn to the disparity in the drug approvals and reimbursement strategies among the different regions.

title: Influence of perineal tears and body image disturbance on postpartum sexual quality of life: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether perineal injury severity independently determines postpartum sexual quality of life (SQoL) is unclear. This study evaluated perineal tears and body image as determinants of SQoL and sexual resumption timing. METHODS: A total of 173 women (2-24 months postpartum, vaginal delivery) completed an online questionnaire including the SQoL-F and Body Image Scale (BIS). Women with perineal tear/episiotomy (PT/E; RESULTS: SQoL-F scores were similar between groups (71.1 ± 23.3 vs 76.9 ± 24.0; CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum SQoL is primarily determined by dyspareunia and body image disturbance rather than perineal tear severity. OASI carries a substantial risk of delayed sexual resumption, warranting dedicated postpartum counseling.

title: Enterovirus 2B protein: From viroporin to membrane stress sensor, mechanistic principles of multi-pathway regulation.
abstract: Enterovirus 2B is a highly conserved, functionally versatile, nonstructural protein. The classic viroporin model, which restricts its role to ion channel formation, cannot account for its interactions with host factors such as Bcl-2-associated X protein, interleukin enhancer-binding factor 2, and karyopherin subunit alpha 1, nor its functional divergence among enteroviruses. We propose a novel, testable membrane stress sensor hypothesis: the transmembrane helices of 2B sense lipid composition and pH changes, and through conformational dynamics, spatiotemporally coordinate calcium signaling, cell death pathway selection, including apoptosis, pyroptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis, and immune evasion. We elaborate on this framework across six dimensions: structure-function mapping, calcium signaling, cell death pathways, immune evasion, evolutionary footprint, and antiviral targeting, along with cross-virus comparisons. We highlight key evidence gaps and limitations, and propose several future research directions. This framework establishes a mechanistic foundation for understanding 2B function and guiding rational anti-enteroviral drug designs.

title: Global, regional, and national burden of exposure to chewing tobacco, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Exposure to chewing tobacco is a known health risk factor but has received less attention than smoking in global tobacco control efforts. As the evidence base linking chewing tobacco use to poor health grows, it is essential to closely track the changing use of chewing tobacco distinct from other forms of smokeless tobacco, as well as the estimated burden associated with its use. These data are essential to inform policy makers who seek to identify and avert the health burden associated with these dangerous products. METHODS: We estimated the prevalence of chewing tobacco use and attributable health burden for individuals aged 15 years and older across 204 countries and territories by age and sex to produce temporal estimates from 1990 to 2023 as part of the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023. We leveraged self-reported survey data on use of any smokeless tobacco products spanning 188 countries globally to inform estimates of chewing tobacco use. Further, we undertook a systematic review and meta-analysis using the burden of proof methodology to generate associated relative risks. Together, these estimates served as inputs to generate cause-specific, location-specific, age-specific, sex-specific, and year-specific population-attributable fractions and the resulting attributable measures of health burden. FINDINGS: In 2023, we estimate 241 million (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 165-355) users of chewing tobacco globally, a prevalence of 3·9% (95% UI 2·7-5·8) among individuals aged 15 years and older. Consumption was concentrated in south Asia, where India had 64·3% (56·1-71·8) of all male chewing tobacco users and 54·8% (47·1-62·4) of all female users. Bangladesh followed with 7·6% (6·0-9·6) and 19·0% (14·5-24·6) of all male and female chewing tobacco users, respectively. Globally, use peaked in older ages, with a prevalence of 5·1% (3·2-8·0) among people aged 60-64 years. Chewing tobacco use was linked to 251 thousand deaths (149-389) in 2023, 152 thousand (96·2-235) of which occurred in males and 99·7 thousand (53·2-164) in females. When adding years of life lost to disability, the total burden attributed to chewing tobacco use was 6·48 million (3·96-9·91) disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in 2023. This burden corresponds to 133·5 (85·8-201·8) DALYs per 100 000 males and 66·9 (35·6-109·9) DALYs per 100 000 females. The burden attributable to chewing tobacco was linked to six outcomes, the largest of which was stroke (55·9 [29·0-92·9] DALYs per 100 000 individuals attributable to chewing tobacco) followed by lip and oral cavity cancer (17·4 [11·3-24·3] DALYs per 100 000). However, the underlying epidemiological evidence ranges from moderate to weak. INTERPRETATION: We observed little change over time in the prevalence of chewing tobacco use, accompanied by a growing burden of associated death and disability. This burden of stroke and head and neck cancers is seen most heavily in south Asia. Chewing tobacco remains an understudied risk factor of public health concern and requires signatories of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control to increase efforts to reduce exposure alongside those made to mitigate the harms of other tobacco products. FUNDING: Bloomberg Philanthropies and Gates Foundation.

title: A prognostic model for use at labour onset to estimate the risk of severe fetal compromise at birth: a retrospective, model development and validation study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Absence of reliable risk assessment and monitoring of fetal wellbeing during labour remains a major clinical challenge worldwide. Cardiotocography (CTG) is commonly used to monitor the fetal heart rate, but its misinterpretation or delays in clinical escalation contribute to poor birth outcomes. We aimed to develop a novel prognostic model for the prediction of severe fetal compromise at birth, combining known clinical risk factors with the first 20 min of CTG monitoring. METHODS: In this retrospective, model development and validation study, we used routinely collected, fully anonymised maternity data from three databases: the John Radcliffe Hospital (Oxford, UK; 1993-2024; model training and testing), the Rosie Hospital (Cambridge, UK; 2016-22; external validation), and the Stockholm-Gotland region (Sweden; 2018-20; independent external validation). Oxford and Cambridge datasets were accessed from maternity and neonatal unit electronic health records; Stockholm-Gotland data were accessed as part of the larger Stockholm-Gotland Perinatal Cohort. Singleton births at 36 weeks and 0 days of gestation or more undergoing intrapartum CTG monitoring, whether labour was spontaneous or induced, were included. Clinical risk factors used for model development were maternal age, gestational age, nulliparity, pre-eclampsia, diabetes in pregnancy, thick meconium, and maximal recorded maternal temperature in labour. Quantitative CTG features included in the model were fetal heart rate baseline, short-term variability, decelerative capacity, number of accelerations, and number of prolonged decelerations, and were extracted using the Oxford intrapartum computer-based algorithms. Birth outcomes were defined in three mutually exclusive groups: severe compromise, intermediate compromise, and healthy. Fit4Labour risk score (ie, estimated probability of severe compromise) was stratified into four risk groups: >95th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, >85th and ≤95th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, >25th and ≤85th centile of Fit4Labour risk score, and ≤25th centile of Fit4Labour risk score. Model accuracy was assessed by use of partial receiver operating characteristic curves and comparison with a clinical benchmark (sensitivity at 15% screen-positive rate). FINDINGS: 147 350 births with at least 20 min of CTG data were analysed: 91 378 from Oxford 1993-2024 (73 443 for training and testing [Oxford 1993-2019] and 17 935 for internal validation [Oxford 2020-24]), 14 709 from Cambridge 2016-22 (external validation), and 41 263 from Stockholm-Gotland 2018-20 (independent external validation). The rate of severe compromise was higher in the highest-risk group (>95th centile) than in the lowest-risk group (≤25th centile) across all validation datasets: 0·9% (95% CI 0·28-1·51) in the highest risk group versus 0·1% (0·01-0·21) in the lowest-risk group in the Oxford 2020-24 dataset; 0·3% (0·00-0·65) versus 0·1% (0·00-0·22) in the Cambridge 2016-22 dataset; and 0·9% (0·47-1·27) versus 0·2% (0·08-0·23) in the Stockholm-Gotland 2018-20 dataset. At a fixed screen-positive rate of 15%, 20-min Fit4Labour had a sensitivity of 33·4% (95% CI 28·31-38·56), compared with the clinical benchmark sensitivity of 39·9% (95% CI 32·59-47·18, p=0·18), and showed consistent performance across all validation datasets. INTERPRETATION: Fit4Labour is a robust prognostic model, readily applicable around labour onset and extensively validated with retrospective data from sites with different maternity demographics and clinical care practices. Fit4Labour relies on routinely available data and could produce interpretable output in real time, providing timely individualised risk stratification that is data-driven, objective, and reproducible. FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research.

title: 2022 WHO estimates for overall and human papillomavirus test-based cervical cancer screening coverage worldwide: a review and synthetic analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Regularly updated global estimates are needed to monitor progress in cervical cancer screening, a key pillar of WHO's strategy to eliminate cervical cancer. We aimed to update estimates of cervical cancer screening coverage in 194 WHO member states and eight associated countries and territories for 2022, including the first global assessment of human papillomavirus (HPV) test-based screening adoption and roll-out. METHODS: In this review and synthetic analysis, we used an established method to estimate standardised cervical cancer screening coverage in 2022. We used programme and population-based coverage data collected up to Jan 31, 2024, selecting the sources considered most representative of each country or territory's screening situation in 2022. Preliminary estimates were reviewed through a WHO country consultation (April-May, 2024; with additional responses received until July 2025). HPV testing coverage was estimated based on HPV test-based screening implementation levels, by country and year. Estimates were applied to 2022 populations and aggregated by region and country-income level. FINDINGS: Cervical cancer screening recommendations were identified in 161 (80%) of 202 countries, with 92 (57%) of 161 countries recommending HPV test-based screening. By 2022, global coverage for women aged 30-49 years using any screening method (ie, cytology, HPV test, visual inspection with acetic acid, or combinations of these methods) was estimated at 19% (95% CI 15-22) for the previous year, 31% (26-35) in the previous 3 years, and 35% (30-39) in the previous 5 years; and 38% (33-43) of women had ever been screened. Disparities across regions and country-income levels were substantial: 5-year coverage was 26% (21-31) in low-income and middle-income countries, compared with 74% (64-84) in high-income countries. 5-year HPV test-based screening coverage was 8% (6-9) globally, 32% (25-40) in high-income countries, and 2% (2-3) in low-income and middle-income countries. In the past 5 years, 62 countries achieved more than 70% coverage with any screening method, and five countries with HPV testing. INTERPRETATION: Despite policy updates, overall and HPV-specific screening coverage remains far below WHO's 70% target. Three in five women aged 30-49 years worldwide have never been screened, and 92% have never received HPV testing, with substantial disparities across regions and country-income levels. Scaling up high-performance HPV test-based screening, alongside HPV vaccination, will be essential to accelerate cervical cancer elimination. FUNDING: WHO, Instituto de Salud Carlos III, European Regional Development Fund, Secretariat for Universities and Research, Government of Catalonia, and Horizon 2020.

title: Foundation artificial intelligence models for health recognition by use of face photographs (FAHR-Face): a model development and validation study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Facial appearance offers a non-invasive window into health. We built Foundation Artificial Intelligence for Health Recognition-Face (FAHR-Face), a foundation model trained on more than 40 million facial photographs and fine-tuned it for two distinct tasks: biological age estimation (FAHR-FaceAge) and survival prediction (FAHR-FaceSurvival). METHODS: FAHR-FaceAge underwent two-stage, age-balanced fine-tuning on ten public image datasets; FAHR-FaceSurvival was fine-tuned on 34 363 photographs of patients with cancer. Model robustness (cosmetic surgery, make-up, pose, and lighting) and independence (attention mapping) were tested. Both models were clinically tested in two independent cancer patient datasets with survival analysed by multivariate Cox models and adjusted for clinical prognostic factors. FINDINGS: For age estimation, FAHR-FaceAge had the lowest mean absolute error of 5·1 years on public datasets, outperforming benchmark models and maintaining accuracy across the full human lifespan. In patients with cancer, FAHR-FaceAge outperformed a previous age estimation model in survival prognostication. FAHR-FaceSurvival showed robust prediction of mortality, and the highest-risk quartile had more than triple the mortality of the lowest (adjusted hazard ratio 3·23; p<0·0001). These findings were validated in the independent cohort and both models showed generalisability across age, sex, race, and cancer subgroups. The two algorithms provided distinct, complementary prognostic information; attention mapping revealed that each model relied on distinct facial regions. The combination of FAHR-FaceAge and FAHR-FaceSurvival improved prognostic accuracy. INTERPRETATION: A single foundation model can generate inexpensive, scalable facial biomarkers that capture both biological ageing and disease-related mortality risk. The foundation model enabled effective training by use of relatively small clinical datasets. Routine quantitative facial analysis could enhance risk stratification when traditional biomarkers are unavailable. FUNDING: EU European Research Council.

title: A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
abstract: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: State of the global tuberculosis epidemic: burden, progress towards WHO End TB Strategy targets and systemic challenges.
abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious pathogen globally despite decades of effective chemotherapy. In 2024, an estimated 10·7 million people developed tuberculosis, including approximately 620 000 people living with HIV (PLHIV), and tuberculosis caused an estimated 1·23 million deaths overall, including approximately 150 000 deaths among PLHIV. Men accounted for more than half of the cases, and children represented a substantial burden, reflecting ongoing transmission and diagnostic gaps. Approximately a quarter of the world's population has been infected with M tuberculosis, with immunological evidence of previous or current infection. This population includes groups at increased risk of progression to tuberculosis disease, particularly those with recent infection, HIV, undernutrition, young age, or other clinical and social vulnerabilities. Following 3 years of COVID-19-related setbacks, global tuberculosis incidence declined modestly (1%) from 2023 to 2024 but remains higher than in 2020 and far off-track to meet the 2025 WHO End TB Strategy milestones. Case detection improved to 8·3 million notifications (78% of estimated incident cases), supported by expanded molecular diagnostics; however, prevalence surveys continue to reveal substantial proportions of bacteriologically confirmed but asymptomatic tuberculosis, highlighting persistent transmission and missed diagnoses. 30 high-burden countries accounted for 87% of cases, led by India, Indonesia, the Philippines, China, Pakistan, Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Bangladesh. M tuberculosis-HIV co-infection remains a major driver of mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Drug-resistant tuberculosis threatens progress: of 390 000 estimated multidrug-resistant or rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis cases in 2024, only 42% initiated treatment, although treatment success improved to 71%. Tuberculosis-preventive treatment reached 5·3 million people, including 58% of PLHIV and 25% of eligible household contacts, well below global targets. Persistent undernutrition, poverty, HIV, diabetes, smoking, alcohol use, air pollution, migration, and conflict continue to shape tuberculosis epidemiology. With financing at only 27% of global targets, accelerated prevention, proactive case finding, social protection, and sustained political commitment are essential to eliminate tuberculosis.

title: Part II. Measuring skin pain in humans: Quantitative, psychophysical, and patient-reported tools for dermatology.
abstract: Quantifying skin pain is essential for dermatologic research and patient care. This Methods and Techniques in Skin Research article (part II) synthesizes human-focused tools spanning psychophysical and patient-reported measures. A standardized workflow for quantitative sensory testing (QST) outlines the measurement of thermal detection and pain thresholds, mechanical detection and pinprick pain, temporal summation, dynamic mechanical allodynia, vibration, and pressure; these techniques enable phenotyping of gain and loss of somatosensory function. Core patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) such as the Numeric Rating Scale, Visual Analog Scale, and multidimensional instruments are summarized alongside disease-specific measures, with emphasis on recall periods, meaningful change thresholds, and adaptations for special populations when available. Disease-focused sections outline nociceptive (eg, atopic dermatitis, wounds), neuropathic (eg, polyneuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia), and mixed (eg, hidradenitis suppurativa) pain profiles, illustrating how pairing QST with PROMs enhances understanding. Objective markers such as evoked potentials, physiologic signals, and molecular biomarkers are reviewed, noting current limitations in standardization and clinical adoption. Future priorities include validation of tools across diseases and populations and the creation of guidelines for QST use in clinical dermatology. Together, these methods provide an actionable framework for harmonizing skin-pain measurement, improving trial comparability, and informing the development of targeted therapies.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Partial Injection Underwater Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Superficial Non-ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors (With Video).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Although endoscopic resection is widely performed for superficial non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors (SNADETs), conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (CEMR) may be associated with suboptimal complete resection rates. Partial injection underwater EMR (PI-UEMR) has been proposed to improve the visualization of distal lesion margins and facilitate en bloc resection. We aimed to evaluate the outcomes of PI-UEMR for SNADETs, using CEMR as a historical institutional comparator. METHODS: This single-center observational cohort study included patients who underwent endoscopic mucosal resection for SNADETs between September 2015 and December 2025. Lesions treated with CEMR or PI-UEMR were analyzed. The primary outcomes were en bloc and R0 resection rates. The secondary outcomes included histological diagnosis and procedure-related adverse events, including intraoperative perforation, delayed perforation, and delayed bleeding. RESULTS: In total, 77 lesions in 73 patients were analyzed, including 39 treated with CEMR and 38 treated with PI-UEMR. The en bloc resection rates were 90.0% and 97.4% in the CEMR and PI-UEMR groups, respectively. The R0 resection rate was significantly higher in the PI-UEMR group than in the CEMR group (89.4% vs. 69.2%). Histological diagnoses were similar between the groups. No intraoperative perforation occurred in either group. No procedure-related adverse events, including delayed perforation or bleeding, were observed in the PI-UEMR group. CONCLUSIONS: While maintaining a favorable safety profile, PI-UEMR was associated with a higher R0 resection rate than CEMR in this study. It may represent an effective endoscopic treatment option for SNADETs, particularly when precise visualization of the distal lesion margins is required. UNLABELLED:

title: Feasibility and Safety of a Novel Pig-tail Inside Stent for Unresectable Malignant Hilar Biliary Obstruction: A Single-center Case Series (With Video).
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Inside stents are increasingly used for malignant hilar biliary obstruction because of their prolonged patency and removability. Although reported migration rates vary, migration remains a clinical concern, and deployment in angulated bile ducts can be technically challenging. We evaluated a novel pig-tail type inside stent (X-FLEX ARC type) in unresectable malignant hilar biliary obstruction. METHODS: This retrospective single-center case series included consecutive patients who underwent X-FLEX ARC type placement between October 2024 and December 2025. Procedural characteristics were evaluated for the 26 deployed ARC-type stents, whereas clinical outcomes were evaluated after the 13 initial drainage procedures. RESULTS: Eighteen patients underwent 21 endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography sessions, during which 26 ARC-type stents were deployed. Deployment into the intended bile duct branch was completed in all selected sessions. The median placement time was 4.0 min, and additional maneuvers were required for five stents (19.2%). Among 13 initial drainage procedures, clinical success was achieved in 11 (84.6%), and no procedure-related adverse events occurred. Recurrent biliary obstruction (RBO) occurred after five procedures (38.5%), with a median time to RBO of 167 days (95% confidence interval, 137-not reached). No ARC-type stent migration was observed. CONCLUSIONS: This preliminary case series provides descriptive information on ARC-type inside stent placement and removability in selected patients with unresectable malignant hilar biliary obstruction. Prospective comparative studies are needed to determine its technical applicability and effects on stent migration and long-term patency. UNLABELLED:

title: Gel Immersion Endoscopic Mucosal Resection With Submucosal Injection for Superficial Esophageal Squamous Neoplasms (With Video).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Gel immersion can provide a stable immersion environment during endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR). However, its application in superficial esophageal squamous lesions remains limited. In this study, we evaluated a gel immersion EMR (GI-EMR) technique in which submucosal injection was intentionally performed before snaring for selected small superficial esophageal squamous lesions. METHODS: This single-center, retrospective case series included consecutive patients who underwent GI-EMR with submucosal injection for superficial esophageal squamous lesions ≤15 mm in size between January and March 2026. The primary outcome was the histological en bloc resection rate, while secondary outcomes included technical success, endoscopic en bloc resection rate, procedure time, adverse events, and histopathological findings. RESULTS: GI-EMR with submucosal injection was attempted for 13 lesions, achieving a technical success rate of 92% (12/13). One procedure was discontinued because adequate lifting could not be achieved due to post-chemoradiotherapy scarring. The endoscopic and histological en bloc resection rates were both 85% (11/13) on an intention-to-treat basis. The median procedure time was 4.25 min (range, 2.0-11.0 min). No intraoperative or delayed perforation, post-procedure bleeding, or gel-related adverse events occurred. CONCLUSIONS: GI-EMR with submucosal injection was technically feasible for selected superficial esophageal squamous lesions ≤15 mm, with no serious procedure-related adverse events observed in this small case series. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

title: Flushing-Assisted Saline Immersion Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection in the Rectum: A Video-Based Feasibility Series.
abstract: Flushing endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a refinement of saline immersion ESD in which energy-synchronized saline flushing from the knife tip is hypothesized to disperse micro-bubbles and facilitate more controlled coagulation at the tissue interface. We retrospectively evaluated the technical feasibility of this approach in 10 rectal procedures performed at a tertiary referral center. Complete procedural videos were reviewed to describe treated visible submucosal vessel burden, minor bleeding, episodes of transient loss of visualization, and hemostatic forceps use. En bloc and histologically margin-negative (R0) resection was achieved in all 10 cases, while curative endoscopic resection was achieved in nine cases (90%). No intraprocedural perforation, delayed bleeding, post-ESD coagulation syndrome, or unplanned repeat intervention occurred. Median lesion size was 55 mm (interquartile range, 40-69.5), median procedure duration was 102.5 min (100-167.5), and median treated visible vessel count was 21 (11.5-40.75), corresponding to 1.04 vessels/cm

title: Synchronous and Metachronous Multiple Gastric Epithelial Neoplasms Detected During Index Evaluation and Post-Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection Surveillance: A Descriptive Comparison.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: We compared synchronous and metachronous gastric tumors detected during index evaluation and surveillance after endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), focusing on Kimura-Takemoto O-3 atrophy. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients who underwent ESD. Patients whose first additional lesion was detected simultaneously or within 1 year after index ESD were classified as having synchronous gastric tumors (SGT); those with no synchronous lesion whose first additional lesion was detected later were classified as having metachronous gastric tumors (MGT). Logistic regression estimated associations with SGT rather than MGT presentation. RESULTS: Among 1064 screened patients, 256 had multiple lesions (SGT, CONCLUSIONS: O-3 atrophy was more frequent when the first additional lesion was detected synchronously. SGT and MGT may represent timing-defined phenotypes within a continuous atrophic field rather than biologically distinct entities. Extensive atrophy supports meticulous whole-stomach inspection at index evaluation and sustained surveillance.

title: Feasibility and Safety Profile of Non-anesthesiologist-administered Propofol During Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Single-center Study of 454 Procedures.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Studies of non-anesthesiologist-administered propofol (NAAP) during colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) are scarce, particularly in the elderly. We evaluated its feasibility across a broad age range and identified factors associated with sedation-related adverse events. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 454 consecutive colorectal ESD procedures performed with NAAP in 405 patients at a tertiary center (January 2016-May 2024), stratified by age (<65, 65-74, and ≥75 years). Propofol was given by the endoscopy team as a weight-based induction bolus and a continuous infusion titrated to target depth under multiparameter monitoring. New-onset hypotension, bradycardia, and hypoxemia were compared among groups, with multivariable logistic regression for independent predictors. RESULTS: Mean age was 68.2 years; 54.8% of procedures were performed in men. Adverse events were common but all transient: hypotension 14.1%, bradycardia 14.8%, hypoxemia 11.9%, without procedure discontinuation, intubation, anesthesiologist rescue, death, or permanent sequelae. A composite event (33.3%) rose with age (24.7%, 36.1%, and 39.1%; CONCLUSIONS: Propofol-based NAAP allowed colorectal ESD to be completed across all age groups without sedation-related procedure termination or escalation of care. Older age and longer procedure duration were associated with selected sedation-related adverse events, providing clinically relevant information for risk assessment during colorectal ESD. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

title: Intensive Endoscopic Resection for Downstaging of Superficial Non-ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumor Burden in Familial Adenomatous Polyposis: A Single-center Retrospective Study on Long-term Clinical Outcome.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND STUDY AIMS: Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is a genetic condition that increases the risk of developing colorectal polyposis and cancer, as well as superficial non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors (SNADETs). In this single-center retrospective study, we investigated the long-term clinical outcomes of intensive endoscopic resection for downstaging the SNADET burden (intensive downstaging polypectomies [IDPs]) in individuals with FAP. METHODS: Of 56 patients with FAP who underwent endoscopic treatment of SNADETs, 34 underwent IDPs, and 22 underwent conventional treatments, with a median follow-up period of 71 months. IDP was defined as the resection of ≥ 3 lesions in one treatment. RESULTS: The total number of resected lesions was 495 lesions (9.7 ± 7.5 lesions/treatment [average ± standard deviation]) in the IDP group and 42 (1.4 ± 0.5 lesions/treatment) in the conventional group. No delayed bleeding was observed in the IDP group and one in the conventional group. No perforation was observed in our study. The 5-year incidence rates of high-grade dysplasia, invasive cancer, and cause-specific duodenectomy in the IDP group were 15.6%, 3.6%, and 0%, respectively. Downstaging of the Spigelman stage (SS) was achieved in 50% (17/34) of patients in the IDP group. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that IDP was safe and effective in downstaging the burden of SNADETs, and no duodenectomy due to SNADETs was required during the available follow-up period in individuals with FAP, even at SS IV. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

title: Current Status and Unmet Needs of EUS Education in Japan: A Nationwide Survey Focusing on Screening EUS, EUS-Guided Sampling, and Interventional EUS.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) plays a central role in the management of pancreaticobiliary diseases. However, EUS training in Japan remains highly dependent on the experience and educational capacity of individual institutions and supervisors, and the nationwide status of EUS education has not been comprehensively evaluated. This study investigated the current status and unmet educational needs of EUS training in Japan through a nationwide survey. METHODS: An anonymous nationwide questionnaire was distributed to 120 institutions performing EUS across Japan through the investigators' professional network. Institutions routinely performing diagnostic and/or therapeutic EUS were invited to participate in the survey. Survey items included institutional characteristics and educational practices related to screening EUS, EUS-guided sampling, and interventional EUS (I-EUS). Data regarding annual procedure volumes, criteria for trainee initiation, training systems, and educational challenges were collected. RESULTS: In total, 114 institutions participated. Median annual procedure volumes were 510 for screening EUS, 135 for EUS-guided sampling, and 25 for I-EUS. The number of supervising physicians increased with procedural complexity. Most institutions reported that I-EUS was performed by physicians with >10 years of clinical experience.
